About & methodology

The core architect

A copywriter who owns the thinking behind the words: what the customer already believes, what has to change, and which ad should exist because of it.

Core value

I start from the customer problem and belief, build the creative idea, then write and shape the executions.

I start from the market, the audience, the offer and the action I want — then decide what the creative has to say, and why. The script is the last step of the thinking, not the first.

Strategy before copy. Diagnosis before solution.

Evidence before certainty. Testing before opinion.

My framework

From problem to proof, in five moves

The workflow I run on every brief. Pick a stage to see what I ask, what I do and what I hand over.

Audit the business context

  • Offer, price, guarantee, proof and CTA: clear or not?
  • Where the creative sits in the funnel
  • Working, failing, saturated or unknown?
  • Creative problem — or offer, page, audience, funnel?

What I hand over

The right problem to solve before anything is written.

Tools

Deep IA Research · Ad Library Systems · Motion Creative Analytics · Miro · Claude

Research until I can speak in the customer’s words

  • Customer language: reviews, comments, testimonials
  • Failed solutions, objections, desired outcomes
  • Ad Library: hooks, angles, formats, proof, mechanisms
  • Repeated claims = saturated. Missing claims = territory to test

What I hand over

A usable insight bank and a market map — not a giant document.

Tools

Meta Ad Library · TikTok Creative Center · Foreplay · Minea · Winning Hunter

Map the audience’s psychology

  • Awareness level and market sophistication
  • Core desire vs. what makes her hesitate
  • Current belief → the belief the ad must install
  • Mechanism, angle, framework, format

What I hand over

A concise audience map and a production-ready creative brief.

Tools

Notion · Google Sheets · Google Docs

Write the hook family, then state the hypothesis

  • Several openings around one direction — not random hooks
  • Isolate the variable: pain, curiosity, identity, contradiction, proof
  • Think in beats: hook → problem → mechanism → proof → objection → CTA
  • Before launch: one variable, one hypothesis

What I hand over

A structured hook family, modular script iterations, and precise visual direction that creative collaborators can execute.

Tools

Google Docs · Sheets · Notion

Read the signals, keep what teaches

  • Read the whole persuasion path, not one metric
  • Preserve winners, diagnose losers
  • Expand a winning signal without losing the core idea
  • Document what should become a control asset

What I hand over

The next brief, and a growing library of tested angles and hooks.

Tools

Meta performance data · Motion Creative Analytics · Sheets · Notion

Every campaign should make the next one smarter: observe → hypothesize → brief → create → test → diagnose → iterate → document. This is my method; the reported results on this site are the evidence.

Case study 01 · B2B storytelling UGC

Ecomness — Run Your Store From Anywhere

Signature move. Lifestyle proof → operational burden removed → gated access.

Brand
Ecomness — e-commerce platform for aspiring store owners (B2B)
Role
Creative Strategist & Performance Copywriter
Format
Storytelling UGC (long-form) · 3 hook explorations · short-form UGC · 2 statics
Audience
Aspiring store owners who fear the operational load
Objective
Position Ecomness as the operational infrastructure that lets e-commerce entrepreneurs focus on growth instead of logistics.

The challenge

Ecomness was entering a Tunisian market where a dominant competitor already owned the functional claims — better logistics, better suppliers, better pricing.

The strategic diagnosis

Competing feature-by-feature in an already-crowded category wouldn’t make Ecomness meaningful. The real question wasn’t which platform is better — it was who the platform lets you become.

The strategic shift

Category competition → identity-led positioning. Ecomness stopped being pitched as another logistics platform and became the enabler of a specific entrepreneur identity.

The creative concept

The Lifestyle Arbitrage — the creative sells the identity and lifestyle the platform enables, not just its operational features.

Insight sourceWebExpo field conversations

I surfaced this insight directly from young Tunisian drop-shippers at WebExpo: the real driver wasn’t a better platform — it was freedom.

One concept → multiple executions
Long-form UGC · Lifestyle + operational freedomShort-form · Curiosity / efficiencyStatic · Identity + freedomHook variations · Different entry points into the same idea

Situation → insight → shift

What was being sold, what customer truth mattered, what changed in the message.

Situation

Growing a store means juggling products, suppliers, stock, website, orders, logistics and customer follow-up.

Insight

The value isn’t access to suppliers. It’s running the business without personally carrying every operational task.

Strategic shift

Turn a feature stack into one simple promise: less operational burden, more room to grow.

My field insightIn conversations with young Tunisian drop-shippers at WebExpo, I found the real driver wasn’t a better platform — it was freedom. I built “The Lifestyle Arbitrage” to sell that identity instead of a feature list.

The reframe

The belief the ad has to move, in one line.

Old belief

“Ecomness is a dropshipping platform.”

Stop selling logistics

New belief

“Ecomness lets me focus on the business while the infrastructure handles the operational layer.”

Feature

Logistics process A→Z · dashboard · weekly follow-up

Benefit

“I stay focused on marketing & the site”

Outcome

Two stores at once, from anywhere

Creative conceptMy store runs without me being trapped inside it.

My creative brief & visual direction

Production-ready direction, split by the collaborator who executes it.

Format
Short-form UGC · screen-recording heavy · curiosity hook (speed)
Platforms
TikTok · Meta Reels · YouTube Shorts · 9:16
Runtime
≈ 45s

Videographer

Mood
Speed-run energy. “Look what I can do in half an hour.” Clean, modern, credible — not a guru or lifestyle-flex video.
Lighting
Bright daylight from a window at 45° (~5600K) as key, small warm desk lamp as accent; matte laptop, screens at ~80% brightness to control glare.
Camera
9:16 vertical, 1080×1920 min, 30fps. A-roll medium close-up at the desk, eye level, tripod, static; laptop visible over the shoulder, out of focus.
Grade
Crisp, cool-clean, medium-high contrast; Ecomness teal sampled from the logo and lifted slightly above the rest of the palette.

Creator

Archetype
24–35, smart-casual, relaxed — “the friend who always has a side project running.”
Energy
Brisk, confident, screen-share energy. Show, don’t sell — smile with the eyes, no salesy grin.
Pace
Fast-conversational; hit the numbers (30, 10, 24) slightly harder, slow only on the reassurance line.
Rules
Eyes on the lens except on screen cues; script on a phone under the lens; any ad-lib is an extra take, never the main one.

Video Editor

Timeline
Hook punch-in on “30 minutes” → UI zooms at 130–160% through the build steps → empty-room cutaway on the no-stock reframe → sign-up form zoom with arrow + link pill on the CTA.
Captions
White text on a 70% black rounded box, word-by-word highlight, max 2 lines, Latin words keep their spelling.
SFX
Stopwatch beep and click on every cursor action, keyboard-tap bed under timelapses, whoosh on transitions, music dips on the reassurance line.

  • Build — product, site, domain, live dashboard
  • No-stock — empty room, objection removed

Hook test map — same offer, different entry doors: LIFESTYLE PROOF · POSSIBILITY ("you too") · CURIOSITY (social + speed)

Testing mindset Each hook isolates a different variable — lifestyle proof vs. possibility vs. curiosity (social and speed). How I would test this: run each as a distinct ad set against the same body copy and CTA, keep the winner by CTR / CPL.

Case study 02 · Medium-form UGC

Colon Detox — The Misunderstood Body Reset

Signature move. Wrong-Problem Reframe (fat → waste & gas), delivered by a borrowed authority, then de-risked with an "it is NOT a slimming drug" clarification.

Brand
Shifa Bio — colon detox supplement (health & wellness)
Role
Creative Strategist & Performance Copywriter
Format
Medium-form UGC ad script · 3 hook explorations · short-form UGC · 2 statics
Audience
Women who tried diet, fasting and sport — and are still stuck
Objective
Reframe how the audience sees stubborn belly fat, and give her a stronger reason to consider the product.

The challenge

The existing advertising spoke to a broad wellness audience instead of a specific, pain-driven avatar.

The strategic diagnosis

Audience research surfaced a sharper emotional tension: women who had already tried dieting, fasting and exercise — frustrated, not simply looking for “weight loss.”

The strategic shift

Broad audience → specific pain-driven avatar. The internal belief moved from “I’m failing because I lack discipline” to “Maybe I’ve been trying to solve the wrong problem.”

The creative concept

The Biology vs. Discipline Reframe — the colon, not willpower, becomes the explanation for why diet and exercise weren’t working.

Insight sourceAudience & testing signal

My A/B testing showed stubborn belly fat caused the highest emotional friction, which pointed the concept toward a biology-first reframe.

One concept → multiple executions
Medium-form UGC · Recognition → before → reframe → bridge → product → proof → CTAHook family · 3 explorationsShort-form · Symptom qualifierStatic · 2 ad frames

Situation → insight → shift

What was being sold, what customer truth mattered, what changed in the message.

Situation

She had already tried dieting, fasting and exercise. The frustration remained — and the deeper problem was self-blame: “Maybe I don’t have enough discipline.”

Insight

She doesn’t need another diet lecture. She needs an explanation.

Strategic shift

Change the question from “Why can’t you lose weight?” to “What if you’re trying to solve the wrong problem?”

My testing signalMy A/B testing showed stubborn belly fat caused the highest emotional friction, so I moved the blame from the customer’s discipline to the body’s biology.

The reframe

The belief the ad has to move, in one line.

Old belief

“It’s fat. I’m failing at diet & sport.”

The colon is the problem — not your discipline.

New belief

“Reset the system first → diet & sport finally deliver.”

Creative conceptThe Misunderstood Body Reset

  6. Clarify"Not a slimming drug"
  7. ProofNatural · Ministry-approved · 10K+ users · voice reviews
  8. CTALink under video + restock scarcity

CD-C1Problem"I've tried everything"
عملت صيام متقطع نحيت العجين عملت سبوروبدني هو هو ماتبدل فيه شي

I did intermittent fasting, cut out bread, exercised — and my body stayed exactly the same.

Failed-Solution EmpathyShared Frustration
Why it works+

Neutralizes: "this won't work for me either." Names the viewer's exact history before any product appears.

CD-C2Reframe"You're solving the wrong problem"
وماخطرش على بالي إلي كان عندي مشكلة في القولون وبدنيماهوش قاعد يهضم الماكلة كيما يلزم ولا يتخلص من الفاضاتبطريقة منتظمة
short-form
هذا معناها الي الكرش الي عنك موش شحم أما فضلات وغازات متراكمة بسبب مشاكل القولونوهذا الي يفسر علاه الرجيم عمرو معطا نتيجة معاك خاتر تداوي في المشكلة بالغالط

It never crossed my mind that I had a colon problem — that my body wasn't digesting food properly or clearing waste regularly. That means the belly you have isn't fat — it's built-up waste and gas from colon issues. Which explains why dieting never worked: you were treating the wrong problem.

Problem Reframing (Wrong-Problem Insight)Unique Mechanism RevealBlame Transfer (diet → colon)
Why it works+

Turns "diet failed" into "diet was aimed at the wrong target" — the product becomes the missing step, not a substitute.

CD-C3DiscoveryAuthority + symptom match
كل شي تبدل كي عرضني فيديو أخصائية التغذية فاطمة محجوبتحكي على مشكلة ال colon وتفسر كيفاه هو واحد من أهم الأسبابنفاخ وجيعة أسفل البطن قلق بعد الماكلة حتى كان خفيفةومشاكل في الإخراج مرة إسهال ومرة قبض

Everything changed when I saw a video from dietitian Fatma Mahjoub. She talked about colon problems and explained how they're one of the main causes — bloating, lower-abdomen pain, discomfort after eating even a light meal, and irregular bowel movements: sometimes diarrhea, sometimes constipation.

Borrowed Authority (named dietitian)Symptom Recognition — "that's me"Self-Diagnosis Trigger
Why it works+

The viewer checks the symptom list against their own body, so the reframe becomes their conclusion. Named expert as scripted.

CD-C4Relief"It's not my willpower"
فرحت علخر كي حسيت لأول مرة في حياتي الي أنا فاهمة بدنيوإلي المشكل موش فيا ولا في عزيمتي على الريجيم والسبور

I was finally happy when, for the first time in my life, I felt like I understood my body — and that the problem wasn't me, or my willpower with diet and exercise.

Blame RemovalSelf-Efficacy RestorationEmotional Payoff (relief)
Why it works+

Neutralizes the hidden objection: "maybe I just lack discipline."

CD-C5USPSimple mechanism + staged product journey
والحل كان أبسط من هكا نرجع السستام لبدني من داخلبش يرجعو الريجيم والسبور يعطيو نتيجةبديت ناخو deux capsules par jour وهذا شنوا تبدل في بدنيفي الجمعة الثالثة وزنت روحي ولأول مرة بعد سنين نشوف الميزاننقص موش زاد !

The solution was simpler than that: reset my body's system from the inside, so diet and exercise could finally work. I started taking two capsules a day — and here's what changed. By week three, I weighed myself, and for the first time in years the scale had gone down, not up!

Cognitive Ease (2 capsules/day)Staged Progress Milestones (Week 1 → 2 → 3)Future Pacing
Why it works+

The product is framed as the enabler of diet & sport, not a magic fix — the week-by-week timeline sets believable expectations.

2 capsules a dayWeek 1 → 2 → 3 milestones

وبش نوضح حاجة راو colon detox ماهوش دواء تنحيفمهمتو الأساسية يطهر القولون ويحسن عملية الهضمهكا يولي الريجيم والسبور يرجعو يعطيو نتيجة كيما في حالة اي إنسان طبيعيماعندوش مشاكل

And to be clear — Colon Detox is not a slimming drug. Its main job is to cleanse the colon and improve digestion, so diet and exercise start working again, the way they would for anyone without this problem.

Pre-emptive Objection HandlingExpectation ManagementHonest Positioning ("what it is NOT")

Stating what the product isn't buys credibility in a category crowded with miracle claims.

Case study 03 · Long-form storytelling

Soul Dose — From “I Need Answers” to Self-Discovery

Signature move. A skeptic-to-believer story where the sample questions are the demo — the product proves itself inside the viewer's own head.

Brand
Soul Dose — “My Mental” guided journal (mental wellbeing)
Role
Creative Strategist & Performance Copywriter
Format
Long-form storytelling script (VSL) · 3 hook explorations · short-form UGC · 2 statics
Audience
Skeptics let down by the mental-health market
Objective
Overcome skepticism around journaling and position the product as a structured self-discovery experience rather than a conventional journal.

The challenge

The My Mental journal generated real interest, but a meaningful share of that interest wasn’t converting.

The strategic diagnosis

The gap wasn’t attention — it was credibility. A short problem → solution structure created curiosity but didn’t give the audience time to resolve their objections.

The strategic shift

Short-form problem → solution communication became long-form storytelling built to earn belief: interest → identification → product understanding → objection-handling → belief.

The creative concept

The Questions Are the Demo — the product becomes part of its own proof mechanism instead of relying on abstract promises.

Insight sourceFounder co-creation

I worked directly with the brand’s founder to stress-test and refine the journal’s questions, as one of its earliest users.

One concept → multiple executions
Long-form VSL · Interest → credibility → beliefHook family · 3 explorationsShort-form · 2 hooksStatic · 2 ad frames

Situation → insight → shift

What was being sold, what customer truth mattered, what changed in the message.

Situation

An emotionally exhausted audience that can’t say what’s wrong, and no longer trusts the mental-health market.

Insight

The deepest pain isn’t feeling bad. It’s “I don’t understand what’s happening to me.”

Strategic shift

Make the questions themselves the mechanism: the viewer experiences the product before being asked to buy.

My co-creation edgeI worked directly with the brand’s founder to stress-test and refine the questions inside the journal, as one of its earliest users. Mental wellbeing is a sensitive category, so every outcome line below is presented as a personal account from the script, not a clinical claim.

The reframe

The belief the ad has to move, in one line.

Old belief

“A journal is somewhere to write your thoughts.”

The questions are the mechanism

New belief

“A structured set of questions can help you uncover thoughts you didn’t know how to articulate.”

From

“I need answers” — from a psychologist, a pill, a supplement

Mechanism

The questions themselves

To

Self-discovery · 10 topics · ~200 questions

Creative conceptWhat if the right question is what you’ve been missing?

Script anatomy

How the ad plays, beat by beat — and the system built around it.

  10. CTALink under video · "judge for yourself"
Concept · The Multi-Stage Awareness EngineLong-form · Storytelling scriptHook family · 3 explorationsShort-form · UGC · 2 hooksStatics · 2 ad frames
My visual directionI built a slow, first-person “mental movie”: a quiet room, a cup of coffee at dawn. The pacing is deliberately anti-advertising, voicing the viewer’s exact doubts head-on.

My creative brief & visual direction

Production-ready direction, split by the collaborator who executes it.

Format
Long-form storytelling · pattern-interrupt (hard numbers) · product-as-demo
Platforms
TikTok · Meta Reels · YouTube Shorts · 9:16
Runtime
≈ 1:38

Videographer

Mood
Quiet, honest, private — a late-afternoon-to-night confession, not a sales pitch.
Lighting
Late-afternoon window light (~3800–4500K) as key, one warm bedside lamp as a practical; night scenes run on lamp only, curtains closed.
Camera
9:16 vertical, medium close-up, seated, tripod, static; real optical depth — no fake portrait blur.
Grade
Warm cocoa, cream, muted gold, light film grain, gentle halation on the lamp; no teal, no high saturation.

Creator

Archetype
Female, 26–36, natural skin, minimal makeup — someone who has been through it, not a wellness influencer.
Energy
Low-hype, quiet conviction. Raw vulnerability, understated — like a voice note to a close friend.
Pace
Deadpan and clipped on the hook; slower and softer from “3 mois”; pauses are part of the script.
Rules
Eyes on the lens, no reading voice, no acted crying; any ad-lib is an extra take, never the main one.

Video Editor

Timeline
Very slow push on the hook with no music, only room tone → topic cards and a counter rolling to 200 → macro page-slide on the mechanism with real questions read aloud → real verified voice-note screenshots on proof, creator’s voice stops.
Captions
Cream text on a 55% cocoa rounded box; question cards set in a journal-paper style with a hand-drawn underline.
SFX
Soft clock tick and a low sub-bass hum on the hook, pen scratch and page turn through the journey, soft notification pops as the proof cards land.
Moodboard — Soul Dose+
Mandatory creative beats
  • Hook — hard numbers spent on therapy vs. the journal
  • Credibility — specialists, topic count, 200 questions
  • Journey — 3 months, small nightly habit
  • Outcome — lighter, clearer, at peace
  • Mechanism — journal opened, real questions read aloud
  • Proof — 12K users, verified voice notes
  • CTA — link below, judge for yourself

Copy locked — sensitive category: personal-experience claims only, no clinical claims, no acted distress; client-verified voice notes required.

SD-C1Insight"Not knowing why is what hurts most"
هو الي يوجع أكثر ملي إنو تكون تاعب نفسيا هو إنك ماتكونش عارف مناش السبب شنوا الي متعبك بضبطشنوا عندي بضبط نحب نعرف كهو !

What hurts the most about struggling mentally is not knowing exactly why — what's actually wearing you down. I just want to know what's wrong with me!

Problem Naming (cause ambiguity)Pain AmplificationDesire Articulation
Why it works+

Redefines the pain as not knowing the cause — which positions the product as a clarity tool, not another treatment.

SD-C2SkepticismAligning with the viewer's distrust
مزال الواحد ينجم يوثق في مجال الطب النفسي في تونس ولا ولى سوق يتباع ويتشراى فيه وجيعة الناس بالدوايات و les complèment السحرية!

Can you even still trust the mental-health field in Tunisia, or has it become a market where people's pain is bought and sold through pills and 'miracle' supplements?

Common-Enemy FramingSkeptic Alignment
Why it works+

Agrees with the audience's distrust before pitching anything, so the product arrives as the alternative to "the market."

SD-C3Objection"Is it a false promise?"
يمكن الي خوفني موش الفلوس جملا les prixs très raisonnables par rapport la valeur de produit أما خفت لا يطلع وعد كاذب خفت نشري وهم

What scared me honestly wasn't the price — the prices are very reasonable for the value. I was afraid it would turn out to be an empty promise, that I'd be buying an illusion.

Objection Voicing (say the fear out loud)Price-Value ReframeTrust Over Price
Why it works+

Moves the barrier from price to trust — then the rest of the script has one job: prove it isn't an illusion.

ترددت برشة الصراحة في لول بقيت كل مرة ندخل للسيت ومانشري شي[…]شفت شنوا الناس والمختصين يحكيو عليه حتى دخلت لليوتيوب وسمعت البودكات الي خادمينو "فيها خير"..

Honestly, I hesitated a lot at first — I kept visiting the site without buying. I looked into what people and specialists were saying about it, even went on YouTube and listened to podcasts that featured it, which reassured me.

Skeptic-to-Believer ArcThird-Party Validation (specialists, podcasts)Reactance Reduction

The narrator hesitates like the viewer, then verifies — the viewer borrows that verification.

The strategic takeawayThe strongest move was making the questions themselves the mechanism: the audience experiences the product before being asked to buy.

Bathroom niche · shower head — negative command
معادش تدوش إلا و support الدوش هذا عندك

Don't shower again unless you have this shower support

Context
Launched as a sandbox brand for student product testing, then scaled once the creative angles took off.
Angle
Hyper-local domestic drama and negative commands instead of standard product demos.
Psychology
Pattern interrupt → curiosity → impulse. A command that breaks a daily habit creates instant FOMO.
Pattern interruptCuriosityRevealImpulse buy
Reported results$3,200+ weekly revenue · 100+ COD orders/day · 4.5% store conversion rateAuthor-reported (résumé), for two unbranded DTC products.
Strategy in brief

Insight
In saturated categories, attention can come from narrative tension rather than feature density.

  • Domestic drama stops the scroll. Viewers stay to learn why the mother-in-law is furious, and find the product inside the answer.
  • Iterate the emotion, not the product. The winning hook was followed by its positive mirror to reach the funnel from another angle.
  • A negative command breaks a habit. It forces a question about a daily routine.

TakeawayIn saturated categories, attention can come from narrative tension rather than feature density.

Evergreen video ad script · Meta

Flamingo.store

The double-trigger evergreen angle

Hook 1 — the financial drain
تخسر برشة فلوس على تغليف فاليزتك في المطار؟

Wasting a fortune wrapping your luggage at the airport?

Hook 2 — the security anxiety
تخاف من السرقة في المطار؟

Afraid of theft at the airport?

Audience
Travellers buying a protective luggage cover (housse de valise).
Angle
Two durable triggers experienced by every traveller: financial pain and airport anxiety.
Psychology
Loss aversion (recurring airport wrapping fees) and security (theft or damage). The cover becomes a one-time investment and a protective shield.
Durable triggerHookValue reframeProtectionCTA
Reported results3.4x ROAS · 3,500+ profitable orders · 12+ months of continuous profitability from a single creative assetAuthor-reported (résumé).
Strategy in brief

Insight
Bypass temporary trends and anchor the creative in permanent psychological triggers, so it can outlast the usual ad-fatigue cycle.

  • Durable psychology beats trends. Two triggers that don’t expire with a season.
  • The accessory becomes an investment. Framed against recurring airport fees, not as a nice-to-have.
  • It speaks to a fear every traveller has. Protection from theft and damage is the emotional payoff.

TakeawayEvergreen creative can be designed around durable customer psychology.
